description.narrative: The Philippines has relatively strong macroeconomic fundamentals, a high local demand from its 102 million consumers, and steady economic growth of 5 to 6% per year. The middle class is developing. The demand for safe, quality and more convenient food is rising fast. The underdeveloped Filipino agriculture sector is yet unable to supply this domestic demand.Generally, the Philippines' agriculture sector has been neglected and has grown much slower than the overall economy; there have been significant problems concerning inefficient production, agro-logistics and climate change adaptation and mitigation, among others. The Philippines is a net importer of food products. The domestic price level of food is high. On average, people spend 40% of their household money on food. For poor people, this is even higher.With the focus shift on sustainable development, the Embassy is interested in finding information regarding areas in the agri-food sector. That would benefit from Dutch private sector involvement. That would lead to a win-win solution for the Netherlands and the Philippines.The study will be useful for the Embassy in promoting specific agri-food trade and investment opportunities in the Philippines that would benefit from Dutch expertise and technologies that stimulate sustainable development and inclusive growth.In addition, the outcome of the study would provide the Ministry of Economic Affairs with additional information that can help in deciding whether or not to include the Philippines in the field of work of an Agricultural Counsellor. The focus will be given to agribusiness policy issues such as veterinary and phytosanitary market access issues and Smart Climate Agriculture and Food Security.
